raw_text:
Below is a 12-week strength-focused training program for your client (34F, intermediate lifter) that begins 2026-06-01. The plan respects her regular cycle (27-day cycle, period started 2026-05-04, ~4 flow days) and the two flagged acyclic flare windows (2026-07-10 to 07-13 and 2026-08-04 to 08-07). Constraints for flow days and flare days: no HIIT, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping. Outside these windows she is fully cleared. The program uses periodized strength phases and adjusts training intensity and modality around menstrual phases and the two flare windows. I include session details, sets/reps, RPE guidance, and recovery/nutrition recommendations.

High-level approach
- Overall structure: 12 weeks starting 2026-06-01 (Week 1 = 2026-06-01 to 06-07). Three 4-week phases: Strength Build (weeks 1–4), Intensity/Peak (weeks 5–8), Consolidation + Taper to test (weeks 9–12).
- Cycle-aware adjustments: using the client’s 27-day cycle and known last period 2026-05-04:
  - For planning, treat period day 1 for the cycle starting roughly 2026-05-31 (27 days after 05-04). To simplify, I’ll map expected cycle windows each month and give training modifications on expected flow days (4 days) in every cycle. You’ll watch for actual start and adapt week-to-week; where applicable I provide how to adjust if period timing shifts.
- Flare windows: 2026-07-10 to 07-13 (falls in week 6); 2026-08-04 to 08-07 (falls in week 9). During these windows apply the same restrictions as flow days plus extra workload reduction (lower volume & intensity).
- Training frequency: 4 sessions/week (3 strength + 1 conditioning/active recovery). On flow/flare days the conditioning session becomes low-impact steady-state or mobility. Strength sessions use compound lifts with accessory work. Progression is linear/undulating with planned deloads and autoregulation.
- Intensity guidance: use RPE 6–9 on heavy days, but on flow/flare days reduce RPE by ~1–2 or use lighter %s; avoid heavy breath-holding and Valsalva—cue diaphragmatic breathing and shorter sets where needed.
- Warm-up and breathing: 8–12 minutes dynamic warm-up, activation, and respiratory patterning before heavy sets.
- Nutrition & recovery: tailored guidance for endometriosis-related inflammation, iron, pain, sleep, and stress. Recommendations for protein, anti-inflammatory choices, and supplements to discuss with client’s clinician.

Abbreviations and notes
- RPE: rate of perceived exertion (1–10). Use RPE rather than strict 1RM on flow/flare days.
- Tempo: e.g., 3-0-1 = 3s eccentric, 0s pause, 1s concentric.
- "No heavy Valsalva": cue exhale on exertion, avoid maximal breath-holding.
- Flow/flare modifications are indicated in each week’s notes.
- Warm-up: 5–8 min general cardio (bike/walk) + movement prep + 2 ramp sets before main lift.

Overall weekly template (4 days)
- Day A (Heavy Lower) — primary compound squat/variation
- Day B (Upper Push/Pull) — press + row + accessories
- Day C (Active/Conditioning or Mobility) — low-impact cardio or mobility
- Day D (Heavy Posterior / Deadlift variation + Unilateral) — hinge + posterior chain + core
Alternate accessory focus across weeks.

Week-by-week plan
Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 06-07) — Phase 1: Strength Build (Base)
Goal: establish baseline volumes, emphasis on technique and breathing, moderate intensity.

Day A — Heavy Lower
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike + hip mobility + goblet squat x2 sets
- Back squat (or box squat if knee sensitivity): 4 sets x 6 reps @ RPE 7 (3-0-1)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8 @ RPE 7
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 each leg (bodyweight or light DB)
- Glute bridge / hip thrust: 3 x 10
- Core: pallof press 3 x 30s each side
Notes: Cue exhale on concentric, diaphragmatic breathing.

Day B — Upper push/pull
- Warm-up: 8 min row + shoulder mobility
- Bench press (or DB bench): 4 x 6 @ RPE 7
- Bent-over row (barbell or DB): 4 x 8 @ RPE 7
- Overhead press: 3 x 8
- Lat pulldown / chin-up progression: 3 x 8
- Face pulls: 3 x 12
- Core: dead bug 3 x 10 each side

Day C — Active / Recovery
- 30–40 min low-impact steady state (brisk walk, cycling, elliptical) at conversational pace OR 30 min dedicated mobility/foam rolling and 15–20 min guided breathing work.
- Avoid HIIT.

Day D — Posterior / Accessory
- Warm-up: dynamic hamstring/hip prep
- Deadlift variation (trap bar or conventional if comfortable): 4 x 5 @ RPE 7
- Single-leg Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8 each leg
- Seated hamstring curl or Nordic (assisted): 3 x 10
- Farmer carry: 3 x 40 m
- Core: bird dog 3 x 8 each side

Flow/flare notes: Week 1 is not a period or flare window; full sessions allowed. On expected flow days (if period starts early), reduce sets by ~25% and cut heavy sets to RPE 6; remove any breath-holding cues.

Week 2 (06-08 to 06-14) — Strength Build
Progress: add small load to main lifts (2.5–5%)

Day A — Heavy Lower
- Back squat: 5 x 5 @ RPE 7–8
- RDL: 3 x 8
- Walking lunges: 3 x 10 each leg
- Glute bridges: 3 x 8–10
- Side plank 3 x 30s each side

Day B — Upper
- Bench press: 5 x 5 @ RPE 7–8
- One-arm row: 3 x 8 each
- Incline DB press: 3 x 10
- Band pull-aparts: 3 x 20
- Core: plank variations

Day C — Active / Mobility
- 25–30 min low-impact cardio OR mobility + breathing; include pelvic floor friendly mobility.

Day D — Posterior
- Deadlift variation: 4 x 4 @ RPE 8 (heavier than week 1)
- Reverse lunges: 3 x 8 each
- Back extensions: 3 x 10
- Suitcase carry: 3 x 30–40 m

Cycle notes: Expect an ovulatory window approx mid-cycle (~day 12–16). If ovulatory symptoms cause discomfort, reduce accessory intensity; otherwise full intensity is fine.

Week 3 (06-15 to 06-21) — Strength Build with slightly higher intensity
Aim: keep volume, increase intensity on main lifts.

Day A
- Squat: 4 x 4 @ RPE 8
- Pause squat (2s pause): 3 x 6 @ RPE 7
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 6–8
- Hip thrust: 3 x 8–10
- Core: anti-rotation 3 x 30s

Day B
- Bench: 4 x 4 @ RPE 8
- Pendlay row: 4 x 6
- DB shoulder press: 3 x 8
- Face pulls & band rows supersets: 3 x 12 each

Day C — Recovery
- 30 mins low-impact cardio or restorative yoga, breathing practice.

Day D
- Deadlift: 3 x 3 @ RPE 8 (heavier)
- Single-leg work: 3 x 8
- Hamstring curl: 3 x 10
- Farmers carry or sled 3 rounds

Flow/flare: if period occurs this week (map to expected dates: the cycle starting ~2026-05-31 would put period start ~2026-06-27; so unlikely this week). If she reports pain, reduce heavy deadlift sets to 3 x 3 RPE 7 or replace with trap bar high pulls/light hinged pulls.

Week 4 (06-22 to 06-28) — Deload / Technique focus
Goal: lower overall volume/intensity, refine technique, recovery.

Day A
- Squat: 3 x 5 @ RPE 6 (lighter)
- Glute-ham raise or RDL light: 3 x 8
- Step-ups: 3 x 8
- Core and mobility

Day B
- Bench: 3 x 5 @ RPE 6
- Row: 3 x 8
- Light overhead press: 3 x 8
- Band work & mobility

Day C
- 30–40 min easy bike/walk + mobility

Day D
- Deadlift variant: 3 x 4 @ RPE 6–7
- Single-leg glute work: 3 x 10
- Core & breathing

Notes: use this deload week to reset before phase 2. If period falls in this week, this structure aligns well with lower intensity.

Week 5 (06-29 to 07-05) — Phase 2: Intensity Increase
Goal: raise intensity and RPE on main lifts. Anticipate ovulation mid-cycle; adjust if symptoms.

Day A
- Squat: 5 x 3 @ RPE 8–8.5
- RDL: 3 x 6
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 6–8
- Hip thrust: 3 x 6–8

Day B
- Bench: 5 x 3 @ RPE 8
- Barbell row: 4 x 6
- Overhead press: 3 x 6
- Pullup/chin progression 3 x 6–8

Day C
- Conditioning: 20–25 min moderate-intensity steady state (bike/elliptical) — avoid HIIT outside flow/flare.
- Mobility and breathing

Day D
- Deadlift: 5 x 3 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Accessory posterior chain 3 x 8–10
- Farmers carry / loaded carry 3 rounds

Cycle note: This week ends 07-05. Expect next cycle period to start around ~06-27 + 27 = ~07-24 so not during flare. Full intensity permitted.

Week 6 (07-06 to 07-12) — Intensity Phase with first flare window 07-10 to 07-13
Goal: maintain progress early in week; reduce volume/intensity and avoid prohibited activities during flare window (07-10 to 07-13). The flare window overlaps end of week 6 and start of week 7; treat days 07-10 to 07-12 (and 07-13) as flare days.

Plan:
- 07-06–07-09 (Tue–Fri-ish): keep regular training but moderate intensity—main lifts at RPE 7–8, reduce top-end pushing.
- 07-10–07-13: modify training significantly: no heavy Valsalva, no jumping, no HIIT. Convert sessions in this window to low-load, low-impact strength, mobility and breathing, and isometric/slow concentric work.

Week 6 Sessions (split by calendar):
Day A (07-06)
- Squat: 4 x 4 @ RPE 7 (avoid pushing to failure)
- RDL: 3 x 6
- Step-ups: 3 x 8
- Core mobility

Day B (07-08)
- Bench: 4 x 5 @ RPE 7
- Row: 4 x 6–8
- DB press: 3 x 8
- Face pulls

Day C (07-09)
- Light conditioning: 20–30 min steady-state bike/walk + mobility

Day D (07-10 — within flare window)
Modified session (safe alternative)
- Warm-up: 10 min gentle movement + breathing (no heavy breath-holding)
- Goblet squat (light): 3 x 10 @ RPE 5–6 (no jumping)
- Glute bridge: 3 x 12 (controlled)
- Seated cable row: 3 x 12
- Banded pull-aparts / face pulls: 3 x 15
- Core: dead-bug 3 x 8
- Finish: 10–15 min guided breathing and pelvic floor-friendly mobilization
Notes: Keep intensity low, inter-set rest longer, and stop if pain increases. Use RPE 5–6.

If client feels well during flare days, they can perform the modified sessions; if symptoms worsen, switch to complete rest and focus on sleep, heat, and pain management per clinician advice.

Week 7 (07-13 to 07-19) — Return to intensity, autoregulate
- 07-13 is still within flare window; treat similar to 07-10 session (modified). From 07-14 onwards return to Phase 2 intensity but start slightly reduced (RPE 7–8) and monitor symptoms.

Days (examples)
- Day A (07-14): Squat 4 x 4 @ RPE 7–8
- Day B (07-16): Bench 4 x 4–5 @ RPE 7–8
- Day C (07-17): Active recovery
- Day D (07-19): Trap bar deadlift 4 x 4 @ RPE 7–8

Cycle note: Period expected around ~07-24, so not in this week.

Week 8 (07-20 to 07-26) — Peak Intensity then taper into period
Goal: push main lifts this week modestly, then drop intensity if period begins around 07-24.

Days 07-20 to 07-23 (pre-period)
- Day A: Squat heavy singles/doubles or 3 x 2 @ RPE 8.5–9 if client is feeling strong OR 4 x 3 @ RPE 8 (choose conservative).
- Day B: Bench 4 x 3–4 @ RPE 8.5
- Day C: Active recovery or mobility
- Day D: Deadlift: 4 x 3 @ RPE 8.5

If period starts on or around 07-24 (expected 4 flow days 07-24 to 07-27):
- Convert any scheduled heavy sessions falling on flow days to modified low-impact sessions (similar to flare modifications): reduce load to RPE 5–6, remove heavy Valsalva, no jumping or HIIT. Consider doing technique work, tempo lifts at lighter load (e.g., 3 x 8 goblet squat), longer rest and breathing emphasis.

Week 9 (07-27 to 08-02) — Consolidation + deload depending on period end
If her flow ends ~07-27, from 07-28 onwards she’s cleared. This week focuses on rebuilding volume and preparing for next flare 08-04 to 08-07.

Plan:
- Days 07-27–08-03: moderate volume (3–4 sets main lifts, RPE 7–8).
- Avoid scheduling maximal attempts. Prioritize recovery and sleep before upcoming flare.

Example sessions:
Day A: Squat 4 x 5 @ RPE 7
Day B: Bench 4 x 5 @ RPE 7
Day C: Active recovery 30 min low-impact
Day D: Deadlift 4 x 5 @ RPE 7

Week 10 (08-03 to 08-09) — Flare window 08-04 to 08-07 in this week
- 08-03: normal but conservative session (RPE 7)
- 08-04 to 08-07: flare days — apply same restrictions as prior flare: no HIIT, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping. Convert sessions during these days to low-load controlled strength, higher rep tempo work or mobility.
- 08-08–08-09: resume normal training if symptoms remit; gradually increase intensity back to RPE 7–8.

Example schedule for the week:
08-03 (Day A): Squat 4 x 4 @ RPE 7
08-05 (within flare): Modified session — goblet squats 3 x 12 @ RPE 5–6, seated rows 3 x 12, glute bridges 3 x 15, breathing/mobility.
08-07 (within flare): light mobility or rest
08-08 (Day D): Deadlift variant 3 x 5 @ RPE 7 (if feeling well)

If symptoms persist after flare, extend the lower-intensity period by 3–7 days and prioritize recovery.

Week 11 (08-10 to 08-16) — Rebuilding volume/intensity
Return to heavier work if cleared and symptom-free. Increase to RPE 8 for main lifts; focus on technique and consistent progress.

Day A: Squat 5 x 4 @ RPE 8
Day B: Bench 5 x 4 @ RPE 8
Day C: Active recovery (bike/walk + mobility)
Day D: Deadlift 5 x 3–4 @ RPE 8

Week 12 (08-17 to 08-23) — Final consolidation + testing (or tapered peak)
Goal: consolidate gains and test 3–5RM or leave as a heavy week depending on client preference and symptom status.

Option A — Test (if symptom-free and feeling strong)
- Day A: Work up to a heavy 3-rep squat, then back-off 2 sets @ 80% of that
- Day B: Work up to heavy 3–5 rep bench
- Day D: Work up to heavy 3–5 rep deadlift
Keep accessory volume moderate and allow 48–72 hours between maximal attempts.

Option B — Maintain heavy but not test
- Squat: 3 x 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Bench: 3 x 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Deadlift: 3 x 3 @ RPE 8.5
- Accessories 2–3 sets each

If a period or flare falls in Week 12, follow flow/flare modifications (reduce intensity/volume, no heavy Valsalva/jumping/HIIT).

Progression and autoregulation
- Increase load ~2.5–5% week-to-week on main lifts when RPE feels 1–1.5 below target at prescribed reps.
- If client reports elevated pain/fatigue, reduce load/sets by 10–30% and prioritize mobility and sleep.
- Use RPE not absolute 1RM percentages around flare/flow days.

Specific exercise selection alternatives (use if pain, clinician restrictions, or equipment limits)
- Swap back squat for front squat or goblet squat
- Swap conventional deadlift for trap-bar deadlift or kettlebell Romanian deadlift
- Replace bench press with incline DB press or push-up progression
- Replace jumping/plyo with mobility drills and light explosive but non-jumping moves (e.g., fast concentric medicine ball chest pass while seated — only if comfortable)

Nutrition and recovery recommendations (discuss with client’s clinician)
- Protein: aim 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight daily to support muscle repair (adjust per client body weight).
- Energy: maintain slight calorie surplus (if goal is strength/gain) or maintenance if performance-focused. Avoid prolonged calorie deficit around flare/flow when pain and fatigue may be worse.
- Anti-inflammatory dietary choices: emphasize omega-3 rich foods (fatty fish, flax), plenty of vegetables, berries, turmeric, ginger, and limit processed foods and high trans-fat intake where possible.
- Iron: monitor iron status (ferritin) especially with heavy flow; consider discussing supplementation with her physician if ferritin is low.
- Supplements to consider (only after clinician approval): omega-3, vitamin D (if low), magnesium for sleep/muscle cramps, and curcumin for inflammation. Always confirm with medical team.
- Hydration: maintain good hydration; heat therapy (warm baths) and gentle abdominal massage may help during flare/period.

Pelvic floor & breathing
- Include daily breathing practice (5–10 min) focusing on diaphragmatic breath and pelvic floor relaxation techniques, especially on flare/flow days.
- Avoid heavy Valsalva. Coach inhalation before eccentric and controlled exhale during concentric, keep bracing but not breath-holding.

Pain monitoring and red flags
- If sharp or escalating pelvic pain occurs with exercise, stop and consult her clinician.
- If new neurological signs, fever, heavy bleeding beyond her standard, or signs of infection occur (post-laparoscopy follow-up window present), pause training and refer to medical care.

Practical scheduling example (calendar highlights)
- 06-01 start week 1 → follow weeks 1–4 as above.
- Note the 07-10–07-13 and 08-04–08-07 flare windows; plan low-intensity sessions on those specific dates.
- Anticipate flow days ~every 27 days for 4 days; plan lighter sessions during those days (I gave guidance for expected weeks).

Coaching cues and session delivery
- Always begin with a structured warm-up that includes breathing patterns and pelvic-floor friendly activation.
- Encourage client to rate pain and energy before each session; use that to autoregulate (if pain up, reduce sets by 30–50% and avoid heavy single-rep work).
- For heavy lifts, use submaximal intensities in weeks around period/flare or replace with higher-rep, lower-load tempos.

If you want
- I can convert this program into a 12-week printable weekly calendar with daily entries (including exact dates mapped to the client’s cycle), or
- Provide alternative 3-day or 5-day-per-week splits, or
- Provide sample warm-up and a 10–15 minute breathing/pelvic-floor routine to use on flow/flare days.

Tell me which of those you’d like and I’ll produce it mapped to the exact dates.
